title: Hello, Yuma-san!
short: First greetings, asking for repetition, and everyday reactions.
goal: Introduce yourself and use simple greetings and polite classroom phrases.
label: Greetings

sentences.tip: The polite form of おはよう.
A simple check-in question.

sentences.jp: もう一度お願いします。
sentences.tip: Useful when you need Yuma-san to repeat something.
めっちゃ is casual Kansai-flavored emphasis.

focus.label: Useful requests
focus.jp: もう一度お願いします

upnext: X は Y です (X is Y) was the next step.

title: Let me introduce myself
short: Introduce your nationality, work, hobbies, and learn positive and negative です.
goal: Make positive X は Y です and negative X は Y じゃないです sentences.
label: Self-introduction

sentences.tip: The subject “I” is understood from context.
The basic X は Y です pattern.

sentences.jp: 私は先生じゃないです。
sentences.tip: じゃないです negates a noun sentence.
A question listed in the Lesson 1 notes.

focus.label: Negative
focus.jp: X は Y じゃないです

upnext: X が好きです / X が好きじゃないです.

title: How do you say it?
short: Ask what something is called in Japanese or English, and say when you understand.
goal: Use X は日本語で何ですか / 英語で何ですか and わかりません.
label: Language questions

vocab.meaning: I do not understand / I’m not sure

sentences.jp: これは日本語で何ですか？
sentences.romaji: Kore wa nihongo de nan desu ka?
sentences.en: What is this called in Japanese?
sentences.tip: The key translation-question pattern in Yuma-san’s notes.
Polite. Casual version: わからない.
A handy answer when Yuma explains something.
Example from Lesson 2 vocabulary.
Example from Lesson 2 vocabulary.

focus.label: Japanese translation
focus.jp: X は日本語で何ですか？
focus.romaji: X wa nihongo de nan desu ka?

focus.label: English translation
focus.jp: X は英語で何ですか？
focus.romaji: X wa eigo de nan desu ka?

focus.label: Polite / casual
focus.jp: わかりません / わからない

upnext: X が好きです / X が好きじゃないです.

title: What do you like?
ja: 好きです・好きじゃないです
short: Talk about likes, negative descriptions, yesterday’s weather, and past-tense です.
goal: Practice 好きです, 好きじゃないです, でした and じゃなかったです.
label: Likes & past です

sentences.en: Tomorrow is a workday for me.
sentences.tip: Example from Yuma-san’s lesson.
でした makes a noun sentence past positive.
曇り (くもり) means cloudy weather.
寒い is an い-adjective.

sentences.jp: 昨日は休みじゃなかったです。
sentences.en: Yesterday was not a day off.
sentences.tip: Extra practice for the past negative pattern.

upnext: Basic verbs: present positive ます and present negative ません.

title: Everyday actions
theme: Basic verbs: ます / ません
short: Practice eating, drinking, watching, listening, and how often things happen.
goal: Use present positive ～ます and negative ～ません with daily habits.
label: Present-tense verbs

sentences.tip: The basic polite present affirmative.
時々 means sometimes.

sentences.jp: あんまりお酒を飲みません。
sentences.en: I do not drink much alcohol.
sentences.tip: あんまり is often paired with a negative verb.
聞きます means listen or ask, depending on context.
Example in the notes, using 疲れました.

focus.label: Present negative
focus.en: do not eat → 食べません (tabemasen)

focus.label: Frequency
focus.jp: 毎日・時々・あんまり・全然
focus.en: Every day · sometimes · not very · not at all

title: What did you do?
short: Learn cooking, traveling, driving, studying, singing, and using ました / ませんでした.
goal: Use polite past positive ～ました and past negative ～ませんでした.
label: Past-tense verbs

sentences.tip: 料理する combines a noun with する.
Example in the notes.

sentences.jp: 昨日勉強しませんでした。
sentences.tip: Past negative ～ませんでした.

parts.kana: べんきょうしませんでした

sentences.tip: 歌 is the noun “song”; 歌う is the verb.

sentences.jp: 今年三回日本に行きました。
sentences.en: I went to Japan three times this year.
sentences.tip: An example from Yuma-san’s notes for 三回.

sentences.jp: 来年名古屋に行きます。
sentences.en: I will go to Nagoya next year.
sentences.tip: A future statement with polite ます.

focus.label: Past negative
focus.en: did not · 勉強しませんでした

focus.label: Basic verb family
focus.jp: 料理する・旅行する・運転する・勉強する
focus.romaji: ryouri suru · ryokou suru · unten suru · benkyou suru

title: Numbers & telling time
short: Learn numbers, special hour readings, half past, and the times you wake up or sleep.
goal: Read clock times and use [time] に [verb] for daily routines.
label: Numbers & clock time

sentences.jp: 昨日何時に寝ましたか？
sentences.en: What time did you go to sleep yesterday?
sentences.tip: The question from Yuma-san’s notes. に marks the specific time.

sentences.jp: 昨日何時に起きましたか？
sentences.en: What time did you wake up yesterday?
sentences.tip: Another question from the notes.

sentences.jp: ドジャーにえさをやります。
sentences.tip: An example from Yuma-san’s notes!

sentences.en: I make a dish / cook food.
sentences.tip: An example in the notes for 作ります.
Uses 六時半, the half-past time form listed in the lesson.

focus.label: Time marker
focus.en: Do an action at a specific time
